content.GLOSS: Hard rock; the found material a thing is founded on
content.ART_PROMPT: A single undressed limestone block half-buried at the foot of a rising course of mud brick, chisel marks raw across its face, an iron wedge and a coil of measuring cord left lying on it, the red glow of a brick kiln beating across the stone, no people, luminous cinematic oil painting with impressionistic brushwork, saturated full colour, a strong symbolic subject, no engraving or line art, firelight from below, red and orange on stone, smoke against black
content.ABILITY_TEXT: Look at the bottom three cards of the Tower. Add one of those cards that is a NOUN to your hand and put the other cards on the bottom of the Tower.
content.OT_VERSE_SNIPPET: And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter
content.NT_VERSE_SNIPPET: upon this rock I will build my church
content.OT_VERSE_LINE: Genesis 11:3 — “And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter”
content.NT_VERSE_LINE: Matthew 16:18 — “upon this rock I will build my church”
TRIVIA_BULLETS: There is no building stone in the alluvial plain of Shinar, so Babel's builders burned brick for it and used slime for morter - a city of substitutes from the first course up.
Greek splits the one Hebrew word: lithos is a stone a man can lift and petra is the rock a house is founded on, and both stand for eben.
Matthew 16:18 sets a name against a noun, Petros against petra - masculine for the man, feminine for the rock - a pun that works only in Greek.

model_prompt: Generate a premium vertical trading card. Output ONLY the card; no surrounding text or watermarks. NEVER use brackets [ ]. RARITY: Print rarity text then a diamond icon (e.g. 'RARE ◆'). Diamond color: white=COMMON, green=UNCOMMON, gold=RARE, orange=GLORIOUS. All use same diamond shape. COST INDICATOR: Below rarity for RARE show '+🂠' (plus and one card), for GLORIOUS show '+🂠🂠' (plus and two cards). No cost indicator for COMMON/UNCOMMON. STAT PIPS: Use navy circles only, not diamonds. Render: header, stats, ability, OT verse, NT verse, Greek/Heb strip, trivia. Greek/Hebrew must be legible (Hebrew right-to-left).
